policy.scope: AOT, Cranelift JIT, canonical interpreter, Web Wasm/browser, and comptime adapter correspondence for shared operations
policy.foreign_suffix: rustc/LLVM, Cranelift, assembler/linker, browser/VM, foreign libraries, and physical environment remain separate named assumptions at their edges

claim.statement: For every operation and execution mode admitted by the canonical capability relation, this stage binds the shared operation identity to the real artifact, dispatch/control-transfer path, ABI representation, width/layout conversion, handle/callback/result/error/cleanup/task-completion seam, target identity, and tool configuration. It records source correspondence and consumes optional identity-bound positive observation certificates as bounded matched evidence; only an approved canonical formal discharge may qualify a row as proved, and no finite result is universal.
preconditions: The current Core dispatcher, canonical MIR target applicability, artifact plan, and capability relation are identified inputs.
Each adapter route names a real source definition or an explicit foreign edge; a route name alone is not a binding.
Generated Rust, Cranelift, interpreter, Web, and comptime paths consume the selected shared operation and artifact identity without re-deciding semantic policy.
Every current #2941 obligation receives exactly one source-bound disposition, including unavailable and unsupported applicability rows.
Any source, shared operation, target, artifact, tool configuration, capability relation, fixture, witness, or checker digest change invalidates the current correspondence record.
unsupported_cases: a capability relation row that is missing, unavailable, stale, failed, planned, unsupported, or not identity-bound; these rows remain required unless exactly owner-ratified as not applicable
an artifact target, function, foreign call, link, callback, task, or entry that is not applicable to the selected target
a route whose source definition or generated bridge cannot be located in the authoritative source roots
a width, layout, calling convention, handle, callback, result, error, cleanup, or completion correspondence without an identity-bound observation
rustc/LLVM, Cranelift, assembler/linker, browser/VM, foreign library, operating-system, device, allocator, scheduler, or physical-environment behavior beyond its named assumption

execution.resource_policy: unknown, unavailable, stale, and unobserved adapter facts remain blocked; source correspondence is not runtime evidence

capability_relation.join_rule: a current identity-bound relation row determines whether a mode is applicable; its disposition determines qualification separately, so failed, stale, unavailable, planned, and unsupported rows remain required unless exactly owner-ratified-not-applicable

inventory_join.join_rule: a shared operation is adapter-bound only when the dispatcher row, operation obligation, applicable capability row, selected artifact target, real route definition, target/tool identity, and dependent Prelude/runtime records all agree; no route name or tool-presence check is proof

memory_premises.statement: Vetted memory internals may use unsafe operations only behind checked pointer, allocation, alignment, lifetime, and failure premises; a safe-call wrapper does not erase those premises.
Allocator capacity, layout, and release outcomes are explicit resource premises; exhaustion is a typed resource failure, not undefined behavior.
Receiver and callback handles cannot be used after their terminal lifecycle transition; safe calls retain the owner and cleanup premises.

binding_methods.source: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet, crates/jet-foundation/src/MIR.rs, and target adapter source
binding_methods.construction: dispatcher rows, target enum/applicability facts, artifact selections, route definitions, and source spans are indexed without replacing a body by a route name
binding_methods.limit: source binding is not semantic or runtime proof

binding_methods.source: proof/compiler/toolchain/manifest.json, canonical adapter semantic model, and current checked adapter identity
binding_methods.construction: a replay_ref selects a pinned compiler-proof claim whose proposition, implementation, correspondence route, model, and candidate identity are checked against the canonical adapter goal before the shared Lean replay runs
binding_methods.limit: a successful pinned replay qualifies only its exact finite operation/mode record; it does not widen applicability or establish a universal adapter theorem

binding_methods.source: proof/compiler/adapters/models, proof/compiler/toolchain/manifest.json, proof/compiler/adapters/fixtures, optional proof/compiler/adapters/observations.json, and optional proof/compiler/adapters/discharge.json
binding_methods.construction: the canonical adapter model supplies the semantic goal and route declaration; same-observation dimensions, target bridge requirements, independent negative controls, and future identity-bound positive observations remain separately checked, while proved requires an actual pinned replay
binding_methods.limit: finite source witnesses, observations, and negative controls are never universal proof

coverage.owner_rule: every current adapter operation, adapter target, and adapter boundary row receives one source-bound disposition
coverage.qualification_rule: mapped_unproved, unsupported, and unmapped rows remain blocked; finite observations may establish bounded matched coverage but no adapter row may claim proved without an approved canonical formal discharge

foreign_assumptions.edge: RustAot/Web Wasm emitted source to rustc and LLVM
foreign_assumptions.contract: rustc and LLVM preserve the selected Rust/MIR ABI, widths, layout, failure carrier, and target identity under the recorded configuration

foreign_assumptions.edge: canonical MIR artifact to Cranelift IR and resident module
foreign_assumptions.contract: Cranelift preserves declared call conventions, host-word representations, handles, callbacks, trap/failure transport, and completion order

foreign_assumptions.edge: emitted Rust/native object closure to executable or library
foreign_assumptions.contract: the assembler/linker consumes the exact artifact closure and does not change the recorded symbol, layout, or target identity

foreign_assumptions.edge: generated Web Wasm/JavaScript publication to browser or Wasm VM
foreign_assumptions.contract: the named browser/VM honors the generated ABI, linear-memory widths, callback schedule, and resource lifetime

foreign_assumptions.edge: adapter wrapper to crypto, HTTP, font, service, data, and other foreign libraries
foreign_assumptions.contract: the foreign library satisfies its named ABI, encoding, bounds, error, callback, and lifetime contract; its status never proves the Jet wrapper

foreign_assumptions.edge: OS, device, allocator, clock, scheduler, and physical resource providers
foreign_assumptions.contract: the environment satisfies the named target, width, synchronization, capacity, scheduling, and release premises

proven: The checker binds current adapter dispatcher rows, canonical artifact target facts, source route definitions, target bridge markers, and capability-relation identity when those inputs are available.
The checker reports exact source, operation, artifact, target, tool-configuration, dependency, fixture, and negative-control digests without executing the compiler or fixtures.
The checker rejects stale, missing, unsupported, mismatched, or unknown rows and cannot promote them to proved.
assumed: Ratified shared Prelude/Core and runtime contracts state the operation-level policy consumed by every adapter.
Named rustc/LLVM, Cranelift, assembler/linker, browser/VM, foreign-library, and physical-environment contracts hold at their edges.
The pinned jet.compiler-proof.v1 claim identity identifies the candidate without changing adapter semantics.
tested: The source relation, artifact plan, ABI/layout markers, callback/task seams, same-observation fixture declarations, and independent negative controls are checked structurally.
blocked: Runtime execution through AOT/default run/dev/interpreter and applicable Web paths until the retained identity-bound observations are executed by the designated proof workflow.
Semantic equality of results, failures, mutation, input consumption, effect order, cleanup, resources, schedules, and task completion until complete identity-bound observations exist.
Universal correspondence and all named foreign or physical-environment behavior beyond the explicit assumptions.
